subject: Concurrency insurance request for POC throughput & soak validation
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramirez <elena@vectra.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Concurrency insurance request for POC throughput & soak validation

Hi Elena —

Great talking yesterday. As discussed, Vectra's engineering team wants to run a 48h overnight soak at target concurrency to validate tail-latency behaviour before committing to dedicated capacity. To make the soak representative we need to drive sustained throughput for a few million tokens over the window.

Quick ask: can Redwood provision a short-term concurrency insurance package for the POC (48–72 hours) so your team can run the soak at scale without throttling? Specifically we recommend: 
- Reserved burst for a 48h window (peak concurrency up to 600 RPS for the test)
- Short-lived elevated quota so KV cache warm-up is realistic

I've attached a proposed throughput plan and a YAML with the soak config so you can forward to ops. If we can greenlight this by EOD Wednesday your team can run the test Thu–Fri and we'll attach the results to the M&A.

Attachments (stub): throughput_plan_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), soak-test-cfg.yaml (config)

Next steps: if procurement needs paperwork, Marissa can loop in finance for a one-off sponsorship credit. Karthik — tagging you for approvals and a quick note on expected cost impact.

Thanks —
Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ramirez <elena@vectra.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@vectra.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency insurance request for POC throughput & soak validation

Lukas —

Thanks for the clear plan and the attachments. Our infra lead reviewed the soak config and it matches what we need. A couple of items from procurement's side:
1) We need a short statement on data retention and logs during the soak (SOC2 concern).
2) Any contract/credit paperwork should include an end date and a simple rollback clause.

Procurement (copied) will advise on the doc; happy to fast-track once we have the retention note. We’re aiming to run Thu morning PST.

—Elena
Elena Ramirez
Head of Integrations, Vectra AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramirez <elena@vectra.ai>, Procurement <procurement@vectra.ai>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concurrency insurance request for POC throughput & soak validation

Elena / procurement team —

Quick answers to items you raised:
- Data retention & logs: Redwood will retain only ephemeral request metadata for the soak (request timestamps, token counts, aggregated latency histograms). No customer payloads will be persisted beyond 48 hours for this test. We can provide a short one-page attestation and an audit extract post-run.
- Paperwork: I’ve drafted a short mutual-action addendum that limits the elevated quota window to 72 hours and includes a rollback clause. Attached: mutual-action-plan.pdf (one-page addendum).

If procurement is comfortable we can finalize a DocuSign today. Sam Patel on our solutions team will shadow the soak and monitor tail-latency; he can jump on a call Thu morning for ramp guidance.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachments (stub): mutual-action-plan.pdf
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@cloudarch.io>

Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Concurrency insurance request for POC throughput & soak validation

Forwarding live run checklist and runbook snippets we will use during the soak (see inline).

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@cloudarch.io>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 13:55:00 -0700
To: Redwood Operations <ops@redwood.com>
Subject: Soak run checklist (Vectra)

Run checklist highlights: 
- Pre-run: confirm elevated quota applied, snapshot instance metrics, warm caches with 1 hour synthetic load at 20% traffic.
- Ramp plan: 0 -> 60% in 15m, -> 90% in 45m, hold for 24h, then gradual taper.
- Monitoring: tail-latency p95/p99 alerts to pager; token-rate and KV-hit-rate dashboards up.
- Post-run: export latency histograms + sample traces (anonymized).

I’ll be on call Thu 08:30 PST; will monitor and coordinate rollbacks if needed.

Sam Patel
Solutions Engineer (contracted)
